notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.0: the Factory Map, one front door for work, and planning that keeps what you agreed

• Factory Map: every Work Item now opens on a live map of its work — Outcome, Environment, Council, tasks running in parallel, verification and your review — with the step being worked on highlighted. Click a step to see it; proof opens in place. Map, Workspace, Timeline and Conversation share one header. A view you chose stays yours.
• A proof that checked no acceptance criteria now reads "Tests passed · no criteria checked", never a green seal; accepting it says exactly that.
• One front door: a Board ticket started in the AI Factory becomes a real Factory Work Item, keeps its source ("From the Board · S12-T1") and its acceptance criteria, and opens the same Work Item if you start it again — even after a double click, a lost response or a restart.
• The AI Factory composer keeps your unsent request per project. Type / to pick a skill and @ to include a file, folder, ticket, Work Item or watched pull request. Mentioning something never grants access; a reference that no longer exists stops Start and says which one.
• Adaptive planning: a short, low-risk request starts directly. Anything else gets the Coordinator's recommendation — and questions only when something material is unclear, answered inline. What you agree becomes the Work Item's locked criteria and its constraints, carried through planning, retries and recovery; Plan as a project keeps them, criterion by criterion.
• After Start, the recommendation slides in where you'll use it, with one clear Start; interrupted work folds to one line.
• Engineering Memory is much faster on large repositories. On a VS Code-sized repository, an Inspector detail went from 16–29 seconds to milliseconds, and impact from 18–34 seconds to under a second. Opening the Architecture map, finding where you are and switching tabs are near-instant, memory use dropped from gigabytes to megabytes, and the window no longer freezes during Refresh understanding. When an impact analysis reaches a limit, it says so instead of presenting partial results as complete.
• The Architecture map is readable at any repository size, with structure first, one relationship control, plain explanations and keyboard access. A repository indexed by an earlier Vekrun is prepared in the background, with progress and Stop.
• Claude Code reads "connected" only when a real call through its sign-in worked; an expired sign-in asks you to sign in again and keeps your request.
• Rails apps: the database names your config/database.yml reads (DB_USER, DB_PASS…) now point at the test database; tests that can't reach their database are reported as an environment problem, not a failure, and the real error is kept.
• Fixes: Resume shows the work it resumed; Open Agents lands on the coding agents; the stop banner says when it's about another Work Item; the live app's scroll never moves Vekrun; spending caps never let an unknown-cost paid call through.
